# DARING — A Generative Design Workshop · project package

This file is a complete, self-contained copy of one portfolio project from `personal_assistant`. A Claude Code session can use it two ways. It can rebuild the project byte for byte in another checkout of the app, following §8. Or it can treat the project as a worked example of the repo's conventions when authoring a new one, following §9. Every file the artifact route serves is inlined here; only the three videos travel separately.

## 1. Overview

DARING is a one-hour internal workshop for Zemingo's product designers, held on 6 October 2026. It put nine generative-design challenges in front of the team, each outside a designer's usual discipline, and shipped each one as a small starter that already ran on a participant's Mac. For the day the nine became stations around one table: set them up, walk between them, then make something new. Boaz, Design Team Leader at Zemingo, designed the workshop and its look — the DARING key visual and the 3D ribbon built from it — wrote all its content, facilitated it, and directed the build of the starters, their tests and the participant pages with Claude Code.

It earns its place in the portfolio for two reasons. It shows design leadership as enablement: moving a team into unfamiliar, AI-assisted creative territory with working material rather than slides. And it shows a method for directing AI-built software and trusting the result: feasibility first, one contract every starter keeps, automated acceptance tests in real Chrome plus a human check per station, and fallbacks that are labelled rather than hidden. A visitor should leave having opened a station and played with it, and knowing what was and was not proven.

Two rules travel with this project. Faces stay blurred: the photos and videos from the day are published, at the owner's decision, only with every face covered, and a rebuild must use the blurred files in this package, never the originals. And commits that participants made to the workshop repository after the day are theirs: the station builds here come from the facilitator's last commit `e519810`, and the two stations that participants later changed (06 and 09) were rebuilt from that commit.

## 5. Asset manifest

Destination paths are relative to the repo root. The artifact route serves only `.html .js .jsx .css .png .jpg .webp .svg .json`. That is why the three `.mp4` files live under `apps/web/public/media/`, and why the fonts the pages and station 01 need are inlined into their CSS as data URIs instead of shipping as `.woff2` files the route would refuse.

48 assets, 25997209 bytes in all: 45 inlined (5973640 bytes, of which 18 rasters are 4846868 base64 characters) and 3 videos carried separately (20023569 bytes).

**Why the minified bundles are inlined.** The rule for third-party runtime files is to list them, not inline them, because they can be reinstalled from npm. These bundles are different: each is a station's or the hero's own code compiled together with its library (Three.js 0.186.1, planck 1.5.0), and the only way to reproduce one is to build it from the workshop repository, which is a private Zemingo repository a target checkout may not reach. So they are inlined verbatim, and the libraries inside them are recorded here instead: Three.js 0.186.1 (stations 03 and 07, and the hero), planck 1.5.0 (station 06), @fontsource/rubik 5.3.0 (station 01's fonts), built with Vite 8.3.2. No separate vendor files exist.

```html
      <div>
        <h1>A Word That Escapes</h1>
        <p>Type a word. It starts legible, then grows, drifts and connects on its own. You set the rules, not the result.</p>
      </div>
      <div data-error role="alert"></div>
      <div class="row">
        <button id="start">Start</button>
        <button id="pause">Pause</button>
        <button id="reset">Reset</button>
      </div>
      <div class="row">
        <label for="text">Word</label>
        <input id="text" dir="auto" spellcheck="false" maxlength="24">
      </div>
      <div class="row">
        <label for="seed">Seed</label>
        <input id="seed" spellcheck="false">
        <button id="newseed" title="Pick a new random seed and reset">New seed</button>
      </div>
      <div id="stats"></div>
      <p>Press Enter in a field (or Reset) to start over with that word or seed.</p>
    </aside>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

```html
      <div class="row">
        <label for="seed">Seed</label>
        <input id="seed" spellcheck="false">
        <button id="newseed" title="Pick a new random seed and reset">New seed</button>
      </div>
      <div id="readout"></div>
      <p>Try it: press one spot, wait for it to settle, press the same spot again. Compare the two depths above, then press a fresh spot.</p>
    </aside>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>A Machine That Finds a Gait</title>
  <style>:root{--bg:#e9e3d7;--ink:#1d1b19;--muted:#6b645a;--line:#d2c9ba;--btn:#fff}*{box-sizing:border-box}body{background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink);margin:0;font:15px/1.45 system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif}main{flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:flex-start;gap:24px;padding:20px;display:flex}canvas{border-radius:6px;width:960px;max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block}aside{flex-direction:column;gap:16px;width:300px;display:flex}h1{margin:0;font-size:20px}p{color:var(--muted);margin:0}.row{flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:8px;display:flex}button{font:inherit;border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--btn);cursor:pointer;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 12px}button:disabled{opacity:.45;cursor:default}input{font:inherit;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:6px;width:130px;padding:5px 8px}label{color:var(--muted);font-size:13px}#stats{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--muted);font-size:13px}[data-error]{color:#8a1c0b;background:#fde8e4;border:1px solid #f0b4a8;border-radius:6px;padding:10px 12px;display:none}[data-error].show{display:block}</style>
  <script type="module" crossorigin src="./assets/index-BLRDZROr.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <canvas id="view" aria-label="Side view of the creature"></canvas>
    <aside>
      <div>
        <h1>A Machine That Finds a Gait</h1>
        <p>Five rigid parts, four motorised hinges, gravity and friction. Each hinge repeats the same rhythm; whatever way of moving you see comes from the body meeting the ground.</p>
      </div>
      <div data-error role="alert"></div>
      <div class="row">
        <button id="start">Start</button>
        <button id="pause">Pause</button>
        <button id="reset">Reset</button>
      </div>
      <div class="row">
        <label for="seed">Seed</label>
        <input id="seed" spellcheck="false">
        <button id="newseed" title="Pick a new random seed and reset">New seed</button>
      </div>
      <div id="stats"></div>
      <p>Change the body or the rhythm in <code>src/config.js</code>, save, and watch how its character changes.</p>
    </aside>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

### `station-07` — `stations/07-space-behind-door/index.html`

Station 07, A Space That Grows Behind the Door: the production build's entry page (Vite 8.3.2, `--base ./`, so every reference is relative). The dev-only test hook `window.__daring` is compiled out of production builds.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>A Space That Grows Behind the Door</title>
  <style>:root{--bg:#0b0c0f;--ink:#ece7de;--muted:#9a958c;--line:#33363b;--btn:#1c1e22}*{box-sizing:border-box}body{background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink);margin:0;font:15px/1.45 system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif}main{flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:flex-start;gap:24px;padding:20px;display:flex}canvas{aspect-ratio:8/5;cursor:pointer;touch-action:none;border-radius:6px;width:960px;max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block}aside{flex-direction:column;gap:16px;width:300px;display:flex}h1{margin:0;font-size:20px}p{color:var(--muted);margin:0}.row{flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:8px;display:flex}button{font:inherit;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--btn);cursor:pointer;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 12px}button:disabled{opacity:.4;cursor:default}input{font:inherit;color:var(--ink);background:var(--btn);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:6px;width:130px;padding:5px 8px}label{color:var(--muted);font-size:13px}ul{color:var(--muted);margin:0;padding-left:18px}#stats{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--muted);font-size:13px}[data-error]{color:#ffd2c8;background:#3a1712;border:1px solid #7a2e22;border-radius:6px;padding:10px 12px;display:none}[data-error].show{display:block}</style>
  <script type="module" crossorigin src="./assets/index-k_XTJ_Rj.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <canvas id="view" aria-label="3D rooms: click the floor to walk, click a doorway to go through, drag to look around"></canvas>
    <aside>
      <div>
        <h1>A Space That Grows Behind the Door</h1>
        <p>Each doorway leads somewhere that did not exist until you stepped in. The way you walk shapes what comes next.</p>
      </div>
      <ul>
        <li><b>Click the floor</b> to walk there.</li>
        <li><b>Click a doorway</b> to go through it.</li>
        <li><b>Drag</b> to look around.</li>
      </ul>
      <div data-error role="alert"></div>
      <div class="row">
        <button id="start">Start</button>
        <button id="pause">Pause</button>
        <button id="reset">Reset</button>
      </div>
      <div class="row">
        <label for="seed">Seed</label>
        <input id="seed" spellcheck="false">
        <button id="newseed" title="Pick a new random seed and reset">New seed</button>
      </div>
      <div id="stats"></div>
    </aside>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

```html
  <main>
    <div class="stage">
      <div id="mode-label" class="prepared" role="note">PREPARED IMAGES – NOT GENERATING</div>
      <canvas id="view" aria-label="The picture and the world revealed around it"></canvas>
      <div id="caption" aria-live="polite"></div>
      <div id="request" role="status"></div>
    </div>
    <aside>
      <div>
        <h1>An Image That Invents Its Outside</h1>
        <p>Begin with one image, then reveal the larger world around it, three times. Each reveal keeps what came before and changes what it means.</p>
      </div>
      <div data-error role="alert"></div>
      <div class="row">
        <button id="mode-own" aria-pressed="false">Your images</button>
        <button id="mode-prepared" aria-pressed="true">Prepared images</button>
        <button id="mode-live" aria-pressed="false">Live generation</button>
      </div>
      <div class="row">
        <button id="start">Reveal next</button>
        <button id="pause">Pause</button>
        <button id="reset">Reset</button>
      </div>
      <div class="row">
        <label for="seed">Seed</label>
        <input id="seed" spellcheck="false">
        <button id="newseed" title="A new seed: the reveals drift in a different direction">New seed</button>
      </div>
      <div id="own-panel" hidden>
        <p class="own-intro">Make each expansion in your own image tool (ChatGPT, Gemini, Photoshop's Generative Expand…). This page prepares what to give it and plays the reveals. Your images are saved in this folder (<code>public/my-images</code>) and go nowhere else.</p>
        <ol class="own-steps">
          <li data-step="0"><span class="own-name">Start image</span><label class="filebtn">Choose image<input type="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp"></label><span class="own-state"></span></li>
          <li data-step="1"><span class="own-name">Expansion 1</span><button class="own-dl" type="button">Download canvas to expand</button><label class="filebtn">Upload expanded image<input type="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp"></label><span class="own-state"></span></li>
          <li data-step="2"><span class="own-name">Expansion 2</span><button class="own-dl" type="button">Download canvas to expand</button><label class="filebtn">Upload expanded image<input type="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp"></label><span class="own-state"></span></li>
          <li data-step="3"><span class="own-name">Expansion 3</span><button class="own-dl" type="button">Download canvas to expand</button><label class="filebtn">Upload expanded image<input type="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp"></label><span class="own-state"></span></li>
        </ol>
        <p class="own-tip">In your tool, give it the downloaded canvas and ask it to <b>fill the transparent border</b> with the wider world, keeping the centre as it is. Save the result at the same 3:2 shape.</p>
        <button id="own-clear" type="button">Start over</button>
      </div>
      <div class="row" id="live-upload">
        <label for="upload">Your starting image (live mode)</label>
        <input id="upload" type="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp" style="width: 100%">
      </div>
      <div id="stats"></div>
      <p id="mode-help"></p>
    </aside>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

### `station-09` — `stations/09-loom/index.html`

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Loom with Mutations</title>
  <style>:root{--bg:#f4efe6;--ink:#1d1b19;--muted:#6b645a;--line:#d8cfc0;--btn:#fff}*{box-sizing:border-box}body{background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink);margin:0;font:15px/1.45 system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif}main{flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:flex-start;gap:24px;padding:20px;display:flex}.loom{gap:6px;display:flex}canvas{border-radius:4px;display:block}aside{flex-direction:column;gap:16px;width:300px;display:flex}h1{margin:0;font-size:20px}p{color:var(--muted);margin:0}.row{flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:8px;display:flex}button{font:inherit;border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--btn);cursor:pointer;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 12px}button:disabled{opacity:.45;cursor:default}input{font:inherit;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:6px;width:130px;padding:5px 8px}label{color:var(--muted);font-size:13px}#motif{grid-template-columns:repeat(8,28px);gap:2px;display:grid}#motif button{background:#2f4b7c;border-color:#2f4b7c;border-radius:3px;width:28px;height:28px;padding:0}#motif button[aria-pressed=true]{background:#e8dcc4;border-color:#b9ab90}#stats{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--muted);font-size:13px}[data-error]{color:#8a1c0b;background:#fde8e4;border:1px solid #f0b4a8;border-radius:6px;padding:10px 12px;display:none}[data-error].show{display:block}</style>
  <script type="module" crossorigin src="./assets/index-DKtZznnQ.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <div class="loom">
      <canvas id="fabric" aria-label="Woven fabric"></canvas>
      <canvas id="lineage" aria-label="Mutation lineage: one line per living mutation"></canvas>
    </div>
    <aside>
      <div>
        <h1>Loom with Mutations</h1>
        <p>The fabric grows one row at a time. Rare mutations are inherited by the rows that follow.</p>
      </div>
      <div data-error role="alert"></div>
      <div class="row">
        <button id="start">Start</button>
        <button id="pause">Pause</button>
        <button id="reset">Reset</button>
        <button id="export">Export PNG</button>
      </div>
      <div class="row">
        <label for="seed">Seed</label>
        <input id="seed" spellcheck="false">
        <button id="newseed" title="Pick a new random seed and reset">New seed</button>
      </div>
      <div>
        <label>Motif (click to edit; cream = warp floats over)</label>
        <div id="motif"></div>
        <div class="row" style="margin-top:6px"><button id="motif-default">Restore motif</button></div>
      </div>
      <div id="stats"></div>
      <p>The strip beside the fabric shows living mutations. A vertical line there is one mutation being inherited row after row.</p>
    </aside>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

### `workshop-hero-js` — `workshop/assets/hero.js`

The live hero as the pages load it: a Vite IIFE build of the design source `workshop/source/hero.js` (§6, `workshop-hero-source`) with Three.js 0.186.1 bundled in. It draws the iridescent ribbed ribbon procedurally, lit from a canvas panorama in the poster palette, follows the pointer's light, and swaps out the poster image once WebGL is running. Minified build output, byte-identical to `participants/assets/hero.js` at `2eafeb6`.

```html
        <p class="when-note">עשו את הצעדים שלמטה היום. תגיעו עם מחשב מוכן, מטען, ואוזניות חוטיות אם יש לכם.</p>

  <main class="wrap">
    <section id="before">
      <div class="sec-head"><span class="sec-num">01</span><h2 class="sec-title">מתכוננים</h2></div>
      <p class="brief" style="margin-top:0; max-width: 46ch;">בערך עשרים דקות. עשו את זה היום, ומחר רק פותחים את המחשב ומתחילים.</p>
      <p class="note" style="max-width: 62ch;">כל צעד נגמר בבדיקה, כדי שתדעו שזה עבד. את הפקודות מריצים ב־<b>Terminal</b> (Applications ← Utilities ← Terminal): מעתיקים, מדביקים ולוחצים Enter.</p>
      <ol class="steps">
        <li>
          <h3>התקינו את Node.js</h3>
          <p>הורידו את גרסת ה־<b>LTS</b> מהאתר <a href="https://nodejs.org" rel="noopener">nodejs.org</a> (גרסה 22.12 ומעלה) והתקינו עם הגדרות ברירת המחדל. אחר כך פתחו חלון Terminal <b>חדש</b>, העתיקו את הפקודה, הדביקו ולחצו Enter:</p>
          <div class="cmd"><code>node -v</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת הפקודה">העתקה</button></div>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: מופיע <code>v22.12</code> או גרסה גבוהה יותר.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>התקינו את Git</h3>
          <p>העתיקו את הפקודה, הדביקו ב־Terminal ולחצו Enter. אם נפתח חלון שמציע להתקין את <b>command line developer tools</b>, לחצו <b>Install</b>, חכו שההתקנה תסתיים, והריצו את הפקודה שוב.</p>
          <div class="cmd"><code>git --version</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת הפקודה">העתקה</button></div>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: מופיעה גרסה, למשל <code>git version 2.4x</code>.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>הכינו את Chrome</h3>
          <p>התקינו או עדכנו את <a href="https://www.google.com/chrome" rel="noopener">Google Chrome</a>. ב־Chrome פתחו <b>Settings ← System</b>, הפעילו את <b>Use graphics acceleration when available</b>, והפעילו את Chrome מחדש.</p>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: הקלידו <code>chrome://gpu</code> בשורת הכתובת. ליד <b>WebGL2</b> צריך להיות כתוב <b>Hardware accelerated</b>.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>קבלו גישה לסדנה</h3>
          <p>תקבלו במייל הזמנה ל־<b>Bitbucket</b> של זמינגו. אשרו אותה והתחברו (עם חשבון Atlassian, או צרו חשבון חדש).</p>
          <p>אחר כך צרו מפתח שמאפשר למחשב שלכם להוריד את הסדנה, <b>API token</b>:</p>
          <p class="path">Bitbucket ← התמונה שלכם (למעלה בפינה) ← <b>Account settings</b> ← <b>Security</b> ← <b>Create and manage API tokens</b> ← <b>Create API token with scopes</b></p>
          <p>תנו לו את השם <code>daring</code>, קבעו שיפוג אחרי הסדנה, בחרו באפליקציה <b>Bitbucket</b>, סמנו את ההרשאה <code>read:repository</code> ולחצו <b>Create token</b>. שמרו את המפתח במקום בטוח: הוא מוצג רק פעם אחת.</p>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: הכתובת <a href="https://bitbucket.org/zemingo/daring-workshop" rel="noopener">bitbucket.org/zemingo/daring-workshop</a> נפתחת כשאתם מחוברים.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>הורידו את הסדנה</h3>
          <p>1. פתחו את <b>Terminal</b>. העתיקו את הפקודה, הדביקו אותה ולחצו Enter:</p>
          <div class="cmd"><code>cd ~ && git clone https://bitbucket.org/zemingo/daring-workshop.git daring && cd daring</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת הפקודה">העתקה</button></div>
          <p>2. הטרמינל מבקש <b>Username</b>. העתיקו את זה, הדביקו ולחצו Enter:</p>
          <div class="cmd"><code>x-bitbucket-api-token-auth</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת שם המשתמש">העתקה</button></div>
          <p>3. הטרמינל מבקש <b>Password</b>. הדביקו את ה־API token שיצרתם בצעד 4 ולחצו Enter. לא תראו כלום בזמן ההדבקה, וזה תקין.</p>
          <p>זה מוריד את כל תשעת האתגרים לתיקייה חדשה בשם <code>daring</code>. עושים את זה רק פעם אחת.</p>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: אין הודעת שגיאה, ובשורה שבה מקלידים מופיע עכשיו <code>daring</code>.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>מתקינים הכל ובודקים</h3>
          <p>מתוך התיקייה <code>daring</code>. הפקודה הראשונה צריכה אינטרנט פעם אחת (דקה או שתיים); אחרי זה הכל עובד גם בלי אינטרנט. העתיקו כל פקודה, הדביקו ולחצו Enter:</p>
          <div class="cmd"><code>npm run setup</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת הפקודה">העתקה</button></div>
          <div class="cmd"><code>npm run check</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת הפקודה">העתקה</button></div>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: בשורה האחרונה כתוב <b>✓ Ready</b>. ליד כל דבר שמסומן ב־✗ כתוב בדיוק איך לתקן.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>נסיעת מבחן</h3>
          <p>לכל אתגר יש פרויקט פתיחה קטן שכבר רץ. נסו אחד: העתיקו, הדביקו ב־Terminal ולחצו Enter.</p>
          <div class="cmd"><code>cd ~/daring/starters/09-loom && npm run dev</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת הפקודה">העתקה</button></div>
          <p>פתחו ב־<b>Chrome</b> את הכתובת שמופיעה (<code>http://localhost:5173</code>) ולחצו <b>Start</b>. כדי לעצור, לחצו <b class="keys" dir="ltr">Ctrl&nbsp;+&nbsp;C</b> ב־Terminal.</p>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: משהו מתחיל לצמוח על המסך.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>חברו את עוזר ה־AI שלכם</h3>
          <p>התחברו לעוזר שאתם רגילים לכתוב איתו קוד, ופתחו בו את התיקייה <code>daring</code>. אחר כך שאלו אותו:</p>
          <p class="quote">"בקובץ starters/09-loom/src/config.js, מה אפשר לשנות?"</p>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: הוא עונה על ההגדרות בקובץ. הוא רואה את הקבצים שלכם, כלומר אתם מחוברים.</p>
          <p>אם אתם עובדים עם כלי תמונה שיודע <b>להרחיב תמונה</b>: ChatGPT או Gemini, או Generative Expand בפוטושופ, התחברו גם אליו. אחת התחנות עשויה להזדקק לו.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>תנו ל־Chrome להשתמש במצלמה ובמיקרופון</h3>
          <p>חלק מהאתגרים מקשיבים או מסתכלים. לחצו על הכפתור, וכש־Chrome שואל, לחצו <b>Allow</b>. שום דבר לא מוקלט ולא נשלח: זה רק מראה לכם מה Chrome רואה ושומע.</p>
          <div class="media-test">
            <button type="button" class="media-btn">בדיקת מצלמה ומיקרופון</button>
            <video class="media-video" playsinline muted hidden></video>
            <div class="media-meter" hidden><div></div></div>
            <p class="media-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
          </div>
          <p>אם Chrome מציג שגיאה, או שהתמונה נשארת שחורה: פתחו <b>System Settings ← Privacy &amp; Security ← Camera</b>, ואחר כך <b>Microphone</b>, והפעילו את <b>Google Chrome</b>. סגרו את Chrome לגמרי (<b class="keys" dir="ltr">⌘&nbsp;Q</b>), פתחו אותו שוב ונסו שוב.</p>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: אתם רואים את עצמכם, והפס זז כשאתם מדברים.</p>
        </li>
        <li>
          <h3>מחר בבוקר, לפני 10:00</h3>
          <p>עדכנו לגרסה האחרונה. זה מביא גם את דף הסדנה עם הבריפים. העתיקו, הדביקו ב־Terminal ולחצו Enter:</p>
          <div class="cmd"><code>cd ~/daring &amp;&amp; git pull &amp;&amp; npm run setup &amp;&amp; npm run check</code><button class="copy" type="button" aria-label="העתקת הפקודה">העתקה</button></div>
          <p>תביאו את המחשב טעון, את המטען, ואוזניות חוטיות אם יש לכם.</p>
          <p class="ok">בדיקה: בשורה האחרונה עדיין כתוב <b>✓ Ready</b>.</p>
        </li>
      </ol>
      <p class="note">התחנות והבריפים ייחשפו בסדנה.</p>
    </section>

    <footer>
      <img src="assets/zemingo-logo.png" alt="Zemingo">
      <p><bdi dir="ltr">Daring · Dare to make.</bdi></p>
    </footer>
  </main>
  <script src="assets/hero.js" defer></script>
  <script src="page.js"></script>
</body>
```

### `stations-page` — `workshop/index.html`

The stations page, the first artifact and the one the peek shows. Hebrew, right to left: the hero with the live 3D ribbon, the one-hour agenda, "מקימים את התחנה" with the commands to start a station, the nine stations with their briefs (hover shows the English original) and hidden notes per station, and "אם משהו נשבר". Byte-identical to `participants/index.html` at the workshop repository's `2eafeb6` (unchanged since the facilitator's last commit `e519810`). Its footer links to `get-ready.html`, which sits beside it.

### `workshop-page-js` — `workshop/page.js`

The pages' small script: joins the last two words of every text block with a no-break space so no word is orphaned, wires the copy buttons (Hebrew labels when `lang="he"`), the tap-to-translate for briefs on touch screens, and the camera/microphone test. Byte-identical to `participants/page.js` at `2eafeb6`.

5566 bytes · sha256 `51b7a5ae3b1410d7034a7e03d1af4004ab43c140de37b3d3b77f7a9ed2999c47`

Destination: `content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/workshop/page.js`

```js
// Shared by the DARING pages: no orphaned words, copy buttons, bilingual briefs on touch screens.
    // No orphans: join the last two words of every text block with a non-breaking space,
    // so a single word can never end up alone on the last line (English and Hebrew alike).
    for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('p, li, td, small, h1, h2, h3, .brief span, .i-title, .needs, .os-text')) {
      const nodes = [];
      const walker = document.createTreeWalker(el, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
      for (let n = walker.nextNode(); n; n = walker.nextNode()) nodes.push(n);
      // walk back from the end to the last space between two words, even when it sits before an inline element
      let seenText = false;
      for (let k = nodes.length - 1; k >= 0; k--) {
        const v = nodes[k].nodeValue;
        if (!v.trim()) continue; // whitespace between elements (e.g. list items) is layout, not a space between words
        let i = v.length - 1;
        if (!seenText) { while (i >= 0 && /\s/.test(v[i])) i--; if (i < 0) continue; seenText = true; }
        const j = v.slice(0, i + 1).search(/\s(?=\S*$)/);
        if (j >= 0 && (j > 0 || k > 0)) { nodes[k].nodeValue = v.slice(0, j) + '\u00A0' + v.slice(j + 1); break; }
      }
    }
    // Copy buttons for commands (works when the page is opened straight from the folder too)
    for (const btn of document.querySelectorAll('.copy')) btn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
      const text = btn.previousElementSibling.textContent.replace(/\u00A0/g, ' ');
      try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text); } catch {
        const t = Object.assign(document.createElement('textarea'), { value: text }); document.body.append(t); t.select(); document.execCommand('copy'); t.remove();
      }
      const label = btn.dataset.label ??= btn.textContent;
      btn.textContent = document.documentElement.lang === 'he' ? 'הועתק' : 'Copied'; btn.classList.add('done');
      setTimeout(() => { btn.textContent = label; btn.classList.remove('done'); }, 1600);
    });
    // Touch screens have no hover: a tap switches a brief to its other language.
    if (document.querySelector(".hint-pointer") && window.matchMedia('(hover: none)').matches) {
      document.querySelector('.hint-pointer').hidden = true;
      document.querySelector('.hint-touch').hidden = false;
      for (const b of document.querySelectorAll('.brief.bi')) b.addEventListener('click', () => b.classList.toggle('show-alt'));
    }

// Camera & microphone test (get-ready page): shows the picture and a level bar, records nothing, sends nothing.
const T = document.documentElement.lang === 'he' ? {
  test: 'בדיקת מצלמה ומיקרופון', stop: 'עצירת הבדיקה', stopped: 'הבדיקה נעצרה.', asking: 'מבקשים מ־Chrome גישה למצלמה ולמיקרופון…',
  denied: 'Chrome לא קיבל הרשאה. עשו את הצעד של System Settings שלמטה ונסו שוב.', none: 'לא נמצאו מצלמה או מיקרופון. האם הם מחוברים?',
  failed: (m) => `זה לא עבד: ${m}`, working: 'עובד: אתם אמורים לראות את עצמכם, והפס אמור לזוז כשאתם מדברים.', finished: 'הבדיקה הסתיימה. הכל תקין.',
} : {
  test: 'Test camera & microphone', stop: 'Stop test', stopped: 'Test stopped.', asking: 'Asking Chrome for the camera and microphone…',
  denied: 'Chrome was not allowed to use them. Follow the System Settings step below, then try again.', none: 'No camera or microphone was found. Is one connected?',
  failed: (m) => `It didn't work: ${m}`, working: 'Working: you should see yourself, and the bar should move when you speak.', finished: 'Test finished. All good.',
};
for (const box of document.querySelectorAll('.media-test')) {
  const btn = box.querySelector('.media-btn'), video = box.querySelector('.media-video'), meter = box.querySelector('.media-meter');
  const status = box.querySelector('.media-status');
  let stream = null, ctx = null, raf = 0, timer = 0;
  const stop = () => {
    cancelAnimationFrame(raf); clearTimeout(timer);
    stream?.getTracks().forEach((t) => t.stop()); stream = null;
    ctx?.close(); ctx = null;
    video.hidden = true; meter.hidden = true; btn.textContent = T.test;
  };
  btn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
    if (stream) { stop(); status.textContent = T.stopped; return; }
    status.textContent = T.asking;
    try {
      stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ video: true, audio: true });
    } catch (e) {
      status.textContent = e.name === 'NotAllowedError'
        ? T.denied
        : e.name === 'NotFoundError' ? T.none : T.failed(e.message);
      box.dataset.result = 'error';
      return;
    }
    video.srcObject = stream; video.hidden = false; meter.hidden = false; await video.play();
    ctx = new AudioContext();
    const an = ctx.createAnalyser(); an.fftSize = 512;
    ctx.createMediaStreamSource(stream).connect(an);
    const buf = new Float32Array(an.fftSize);
    const bar = meter.firstElementChild;
    (function tick() {
      an.getFloatTimeDomainData(buf);
      let s = 0; for (const v of buf) s += v * v;
      const db = 10 * Math.log10(s / buf.length + 1e-12);
      bar.style.width = `${Math.max(0, Math.min(100, (db + 60) * 2))}%`;
      raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    })();
    btn.textContent = T.stop;
    status.textContent = T.working;
    box.dataset.result = 'ok';
    timer = setTimeout(() => { stop(); status.textContent = T.finished; }, 20000);
  });
}
```

### `workshop-hero-source` — `workshop/source/hero.js`

The design source of the 3D shape: the readable Three.js module that builds the DARING ribbon procedurally. A trefoil knot swept with a cross-section of deep stacked plates (like a slinky), smooth polished stretches, a hole through its middle and thin spikes, in an iridescent physical material lit from a canvas panorama in the poster's palette; it answers the pointer's light. `workshop/assets/hero.js` is this file compiled with Three.js 0.186.1 by the config beside it. Nothing loads it at runtime; it is shipped so the shape can be read, changed and rebuilt. Byte-identical to `participants/hero/hero.js` at `2eafeb6`.

10583 bytes · sha256 `013f4a38553b804f4f21eb5969a6581013d8b569ff2ef68c2f6cd49d53a473c6`

Destination: `content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/workshop/source/hero.js`

```js
// The DARING hero, built after the poster's key visual: a thick, knotted chrome form made of deep stacked
// plates (like a slinky), with smooth polished stretches, a hole through its middle, and thin spikes.
// Procedural Three.js; it answers the light. Edit, then rebuild with `npm run build-hero` (writes assets/hero.js).
import {
  WebGLRenderer, Scene, PerspectiveCamera, BufferGeometry, BufferAttribute, Mesh, MeshPhysicalMaterial, Group,
  PointLight, Vector3, Curve, CatmullRomCurve3, PMREMGenerator, ACESFilmicToneMapping, SRGBColorSpace, DoubleSide,
  MathUtils, CanvasTexture, EquirectangularReflectionMapping,
} from 'three';

const TAU = Math.PI * 2;
const smooth = (a, b, x) => { const t = MathUtils.clamp((x - a) / (b - a), 0, 1); return t * t * (3 - 2 * t); };

// ── The knot: a trefoil, so the form crosses itself into three lobes around an open middle ──
class Trefoil extends Curve {
  getPoint(t, out = new Vector3()) {
    const a = TAU * t;
    return out.set(Math.sin(a) + 2 * Math.sin(2 * a), Math.cos(a) - 2 * Math.cos(2 * a), -1.1 * Math.sin(3 * a)).multiplyScalar(0.95);
  }
}

/**
 * Sweeps a cross-section along a curve. profile(u) → { r, flat, plates, angle, pleat }:
 *   r      radius; flat: 1 = round tube, 0.1 = thin sheet; plates: depth of the stacked plates (0 = smooth chrome)
 *   angle  which way the flattened section faces; pleat: ripples across a flattened sheet
 */
function sweep(curve, along, around, closed, profile, plateCount) {
  const frames = curve.computeFrenetFrames(along, closed);
  const rows = closed ? along : along + 1;
  const pos = new Float32Array(rows * (around + 1) * 3);
  const p = new Vector3(), c = new Vector3(), n = new Vector3(), b = new Vector3();
  for (let i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
    const u = i / along;
    curve.getPointAt(u, c);
    const f = profile(u);
    // deep, narrow grooves between wide plates: most of the surface sits at full radius
    const wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.cos(TAU * plateCount * u);
    const groove = f.plates * smooth(0.3, 0.92, 1 - wave);
    const ca = Math.cos(f.angle), sa = Math.sin(f.angle);
    n.copy(frames.normals[i]).multiplyScalar(ca).addScaledVector(frames.binormals[i], sa);
    b.copy(frames.binormals[i]).multiplyScalar(ca).addScaledVector(frames.normals[i], -sa);
    for (let j = 0; j <= around; j++) {
      const th = (j / around) * TAU;
      const r = f.r * (1 - groove) * (1 + f.pleat * Math.sin(3 * th));
      p.copy(c).addScaledVector(n, Math.cos(th) * r).addScaledVector(b, Math.sin(th) * r * f.flat);
      const k = (i * (around + 1) + j) * 3;
      pos[k] = p.x; pos[k + 1] = p.y; pos[k + 2] = p.z;
    }
  }
  const index = [];
  const last = closed ? rows : rows - 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < last; i++) {
    const i2 = (i + 1) % rows;
    for (let j = 0; j < around; j++) {
      const a = i * (around + 1) + j, d = i2 * (around + 1) + j;
      index.push(a, d, a + 1, d, d + 1, a + 1);
    }
  }
  const g = new BufferGeometry();
  g.setAttribute('position', new BufferAttribute(pos, 3));
  g.setIndex(index);
  g.computeVertexNormals();
  return g;
}

// The knot's character along its length: swelling, flattening into sheets, and stretches of smooth chrome.
function knotProfile(u) {
  return {
    r: 0.95 + 0.45 * Math.sin(TAU * u + 0.6) + 0.16 * Math.sin(TAU * 3 * u + 1.7),
    flat: 0.3 + 0.7 * (0.5 + 0.5 * Math.sin(TAU * 2 * u + 0.9)),
    plates: 0.3 * (1 - 0.95 * Math.exp(-Math.pow(((u - 0.18 + 1) % 1 - 0.5) * 9, 2)) - 0.95 * Math.exp(-Math.pow(((u - 0.62 + 1) % 1 - 0.5) * 11, 2))),
    angle: TAU * 1.5 * u,
    pleat: 0.06 * (0.5 + 0.5 * Math.cos(TAU * 2 * u)),
  };
}

// Thin, smooth spikes: a flattened blade that tapers to a point.
function spike(points, width) {
  const curve = new CatmullRomCurve3(points.map(([x, y, z]) => new Vector3(x, y, z)), false, 'centripetal');
  return sweep(curve, 160, 24, false, (u) => ({
    r: width * Math.pow(1 - u, 1.35) * smooth(0, 0.12, u + 0.04), flat: 0.16, plates: 0, angle: 0.4 + u * 1.2, pleat: 0,
  }), 1);
}

// What the chrome reflects: a panorama painted in code like holographic foil. Narrow rainbow bands that repeat,
// dark navy bands between them for contrast, and thin white lines for the crisp highlights on every plate edge.
function foilPanorama() {
  const W = 2048, H = 1024;
  const c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = W; c.height = H;
  const g = c.getContext('2d');
  const img = g.createImageData(W, H), d = img.data;
  // the poster's palette, in the order the bands run: silver-violet chrome with cyan, pink and gold sheen
  const STOPS = ['#1b1440', '#7b4dff', '#c9a8ff', '#f4f0ff', '#7fe6ff', '#3d5cff', '#1b1440', '#ff9ad5', '#ffd27a', '#f7f3ff', '#a77bff', '#2a1c5c']
    .map((h) => [1, 3, 5].map((k) => parseInt(h.slice(k, k + 2), 16)));
  const palette = (t) => {
    const x = (((t % 1) + 1) % 1) * STOPS.length, i = Math.floor(x), f = x - i, a = STOPS[i], b = STOPS[(i + 1) % STOPS.length];
    const e = f * f * (3 - 2 * f);
    return [a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * e, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * e, a[2] + (b[2] - a[2]) * e];
  };
  for (let y = 0; y < H; y++) {
    const v = y / H;
    for (let x = 0; x < W; x++) {
      const u = x / W;
      // bands sweep across the panorama, bent by soft waves so they curve over the form
      const bend = 0.07 * Math.sin(TAU * (v * 2 + u)) + 0.04 * Math.sin(TAU * (u * 5 - v * 3));
      const [r, gg, b] = palette(u * 2 + v * 1.2 + bend);
      const i = (y * W + x) * 4;
      d[i] = r; d[i + 1] = gg; d[i + 2] = b; d[i + 3] = 255;
    }
  }
  g.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  // thin white light lines
  g.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter';
  for (let k = 0; k < 6; k++) {
    const x = (k / 6) * W + 60 * Math.sin(k * 2.3);
    g.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.7)';
    g.fillRect(x, H * 0.15, 6 + (k % 3) * 4, H * 0.55);
  }
  g.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.9)';
  g.fillRect(0, H * 0.32, W, 8);
  const tex = new CanvasTexture(c);
  tex.mapping = EquirectangularReflectionMapping;
  tex.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace;
  return tex;
}

function start(canvas, fallback) {
  let renderer;
  try {
    renderer = new WebGLRenderer({ canvas, antialias: true, alpha: true, powerPreference: 'high-performance' });
  } catch {
    return null; // no WebGL: the poster image stays
  }
  renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 1.75));
  renderer.toneMapping = ACESFilmicToneMapping;
  renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.15;
  renderer.outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace;

  const scene = new Scene();
  const pmrem = new PMREMGenerator(renderer);
  scene.environment = pmrem.fromEquirectangular(foilPanorama()).texture;
  scene.environmentIntensity = 1.2;
  const camera = new PerspectiveCamera(30, 2, 0.1, 100);

  // chrome with a thin-film rainbow, tinted toward violet like the poster
  const material = new MeshPhysicalMaterial({
    color: 0xece6ff, metalness: 1, roughness: 0.08,
    iridescence: 0.85, iridescenceIOR: 1.8, iridescenceThicknessRange: [250, 900],
    clearcoat: 1, clearcoatRoughness: 0.05, side: DoubleSide,
  });
  const form = new Group();
  form.add(new Mesh(sweep(new Trefoil(), 3000, 64, true, knotProfile, 170), material));
  form.add(new Mesh(spike([[-1.2, 1.2, 0.4], [-2.4, 2.0, 0.9], [-2.6, 3.4, 0.6], [-1.7, 4.6, 0.1], [-1.3, 5.4, -0.2]], 0.75), material)); // top-left blade
  form.add(new Mesh(spike([[1.0, 1.4, -0.1], [2.2, 2.2, 0.3], [2.4, 3.4, 0.6], [3.4, 4.1, 0.4], [4.2, 4.9, 0.1]], 0.7), material));   // top-right blade
  form.add(new Mesh(spike([[-1.8, -1.6, 0.4], [-3.0, -2.0, 1.0], [-4.0, -2.9, 0.8], [-5.0, -3.4, 0.3]], 0.6), material));            // bottom-left blade
  form.scale.set(1.9, 1.05, 1.1); // the poster's form is wide and low
  form.rotation.set(-0.42, 0.32, 0.18);
  form.position.set(1.0, -0.75, 0); // fills the left, keeps the area under "DARE TO MAKE." dark, right lobe off the edge
  scene.add(form);

  // lights: three coloured lights orbit; a white light follows the pointer
  const orbiters = [[0xb98cff, 0], [0x6fe3ff, 2.1], [0xff8fd0, 4.2]].map(([color, phase]) => {
    const l = new PointLight(color, 90, 0, 2);
    scene.add(l);
    return { l, phase };
  });
  const pointerLight = new PointLight(0xffffff, 110, 0, 2);
  scene.add(pointerLight);
  const pointer = { x: 0.3, y: 0.2, tx: 0.3, ty: 0.2 };
  const still = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
  window.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
    const r = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    pointer.tx = MathUtils.clamp(((e.clientX - r.left) / r.width) * 2 - 1, -1.5, 1.5);
    pointer.ty = MathUtils.clamp(-(((e.clientY - r.top) / r.height) * 2 - 1), -1.5, 1.5);
    if (still) requestAnimationFrame(() => draw(0));
  }, { passive: true });

  function resize() {
    const w = canvas.clientWidth, h = canvas.clientHeight;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    renderer.setSize(w, h, false);

    camera.position.set(0, 0, w / h < 1.3 ? 22 : 14); // big enough to fill the frame, a lobe running off the edge
    camera.updateProjectionMatrix();

    pointer.x += (pointer.tx - pointer.x) * 0.06;
    pointer.y += (pointer.ty - pointer.y) * 0.06;

const canvas = document.getElementById('hero-3d');
if (canvas) window.__hero = start(canvas, document.getElementById('hero-poster'));
```

### `workshop-hero-build-config` — `workshop/source/vite.config.js`

The Vite library config that compiles `source/hero.js` into one classic script (IIFE, global `DaringHero`), so the page also works when opened from a folder. In the workshop repository it sits at `participants/hero/vite.config.js` and runs as `npm run build-hero` from `participants/`; its paths (`hero/hero.js`, `assets`) are relative to that folder. Byte-identical.

446 bytes · sha256 `06fb6a561c75fb1072239131d4abfd2aa315eb5e14b5f309bc5b7759d98acc03`

Destination: `content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/workshop/source/vite.config.js`

```js
// Bundles hero/hero.js (and the parts of Three.js it uses) into ONE classic script, assets/hero.js,
// so index.html works when opened straight from the folder (browsers block ES modules on file://).
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    lib: { entry: 'hero/hero.js', name: 'DaringHero', formats: ['iife'], fileName: () => 'hero.js' },
    outDir: 'assets', emptyOutDir: false, minify: true,
  },
});
```

### `workshop-style` — `workshop/style.css`

The stylesheet both pages share: tokens, the poster typography (Rubik, Bebas Neue), the RTL rules and the bilingual-brief behaviour. It is `participants/style.css` with one platform-forced edit: every `url(fonts/….woff2)` is replaced by a `data:font/woff2;base64,…` URI, because the artifact route does not serve `.woff2`. Nothing else differs.

```css
    .dare { position: relative; z-index: 1; text-shadow: 0 0 18px #000, 0 0 36px #000; font: 400 clamp(34px, 5.4vw, 72px)/1 Bebas, Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .01em; text-align: end; margin: 10px 0 0; }
    .sculpture { position: relative; z-index: 0; width: 100vw; margin: calc(clamp(60px, 12vw, 190px) * -1) 0 0 calc(50% - 50vw); aspect-ratio: 16 / 8.6; max-height: 86vh; overflow: hidden; } /* rises behind the headline, as the poster's form does */
    .sculpture img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: 50% 43%; display: block; } /* fallback: the poster's ribbon only, its lettering out of frame */
    .sculpture canvas { width: 100%; height: 100%; display: block;
      /* soft edges: the ribbon fades into the black instead of being cut by the frame */
      -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000 9%, #000 91%, transparent), linear-gradient(180deg, transparent, #000 10%, #000 84%, transparent);
      -webkit-mask-composite: source-in; mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000 9%, #000 91%, transparent), linear-gradient(180deg, transparent, #000 10%, #000 84%, transparent); mask-composite: intersect; }
    .sculpture [hidden] { display: none; }
    .sculpture::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; background: linear-gradient(#000 0%, transparent 18%, transparent 78%, #000 100%); pointer-events: none; }
    .lede { font: 900 clamp(34px, 6vw, 76px)/1 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.02em; margin: 0; max-width: 15ch; }
    .sublede { margin: 18px 0 0; font: 400 clamp(17px, 1.8vw, 22px)/1.4 Rubik, sans-serif; color: var(--mute); letter-spacing: .02em; }
    .punch { font: 900 clamp(40px, 7.4vw, 104px)/.95 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.03em; margin: clamp(24px, 4vw, 44px) 0 0; }
    .tag { font: 500 clamp(12px, 1.2vw, 15px)/1 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .3em; text-transform: uppercase; margin: 22px 0 0; }

    /* ── sections ── */
    section { padding: clamp(56px, 8vw, 110px) 0 0; }
    .sec-head { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 0 clamp(16px, 3vw, 32px); align-items: end; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); padding-bottom: 18px; margin-bottom: clamp(24px, 3vw, 36px); }
    .sec-num { font: 400 clamp(64px, 9vw, 120px)/.8 Bebas, sans-serif; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1px #5a5852; }
    .sec-title { font: 900 clamp(30px, 4.2vw, 54px)/1 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.02em; margin: 0; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .grid-4 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 1px; background: var(--line); border: 1px solid var(--line); }
    .grid-4 > div { background: var(--black); padding: 22px 20px; }
    .grid-4 h3 { font: 800 19px/1.2 Rubik, sans-serif; margin: 10px 0 8px; }
    .grid-4 p { margin: 0; color: var(--mute); font-size: 15px; }
    .bignum { font: 400 46px/1 Bebas, sans-serif; }
    .two-col { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: clamp(24px, 4vw, 56px); }
    ul.checks { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }
    ul.checks li { padding: 13px 0; padding-inline-start: 34px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); position: relative; }
    ul.checks li::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset-inline-start: 0; top: 17px; width: 16px; height: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--ink); }
    ul.checks b { font-weight: 500; }
    ul.checks small { display: block; color: var(--mute); font-size: 14px; }
    table.agenda { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
    table.agenda td { padding: 13px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); vertical-align: top; }
    table.agenda td:first-child { width: 120px; font: 400 26px/1 Bebas, sans-serif; color: var(--mute); padding-top: 14px; }
    table.agenda tr:last-child td { border-bottom-color: var(--ink); }
    .note { color: var(--mute); font-size: 14px; margin: 14px 0 0; }

    /* ── challenge index ── */
    .index { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 1px; background: var(--line); border: 1px solid var(--line); margin-bottom: clamp(36px, 5vw, 64px); }
    .index a { background: var(--black); padding: 18px 20px 20px; text-decoration: none; display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 4px 16px; align-items: baseline; transition: background .2s; }
    .index a:hover, .index a:focus-visible { background: #111; outline: none; }
    .index a:hover .i-title, .index a:focus-visible .i-title { background: var(--holo); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent; }
    .i-num { font: 400 40px/1 Bebas, sans-serif; color: var(--faint); grid-row: span 2; }
    .i-title { font: 800 18px/1.2 Rubik, sans-serif; }
    .i-terr { font-size: 13px; color: var(--mute); }

    /* ── challenge cards ── */
    article.ch { border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding: clamp(32px, 5vw, 56px) 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(180px, 280px) 1fr; gap: clamp(20px, 4vw, 56px); scroll-margin-top: 20px; }
    .ch-side { position: sticky; top: 24px; align-self: start; }
    .ch-num { font: 400 clamp(96px, 13vw, 168px)/.78 Bebas, sans-serif; display: block; }
    .ch-terr { margin-top: 14px; }
    .ch h2 { font: 900 clamp(30px, 4.4vw, 56px)/1 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.02em; margin: 0; }
    .brief { font: 400 clamp(20px, 2.1vw, 27px)/1.42 Rubik, sans-serif; margin: 20px 0 0; max-width: 40ch; }
    .facts { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 0 clamp(20px, 3vw, 40px); margin-top: clamp(22px, 3vw, 34px); }
    .fact { border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 14px 0 18px; }
    .fact h3 { margin: 0 0 6px; }
    .fact p, .fact li { margin: 0; color: #d5d1c9; font-size: 15.5px; }
    .fact ul { margin: 0; padding-left: 18px; }
    .fact li + li { margin-top: 3px; }
    .fact.wide { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
    code { font: 400 14px/1.4 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; background: #151514; padding: 1px 6px; color: #e9e5dc; }
    /* bilingual briefs: the page's language and the other one share one spot; hover, focus or tap brings the other (.alt) */
    .brief.bi { display: grid; cursor: default; outline: none; }
    .brief.bi > span { grid-area: 1 / 1; transition: opacity .35s ease, filter .35s ease, transform .35s ease; }
    .brief.bi .alt { opacity: 0; filter: blur(4px); transform: translateY(4px); text-align: start; pointer-events: none; }
    .brief.bi:hover > :not(.alt), .brief.bi:focus-visible > :not(.alt), .brief.bi.show-alt > :not(.alt) { opacity: 0; filter: blur(4px); transform: translateY(-4px); }
    .brief.bi:hover .alt, .brief.bi:focus-visible .alt, .brief.bi.show-alt .alt { opacity: 1; filter: none; transform: none; }
    .brief.bi:focus-visible { box-shadow: -14px 0 0 -12px #b98cff; }
    .lang-hint { margin: -10px 0 26px; }
    .lang-hint .he-word, .lang-hint .alt-word { font-family: Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0; }
    .needs { margin: 22px 0 0; color: #d5d1c9; font-size: 15.5px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding-top: 14px; max-width: 46ch; }
    .needs .eyebrow { margin-inline-end: 10px; }
    .callout { border-left: 2px solid; padding: 10px 14px; margin-top: 16px; font-size: 15px; color: #d5d1c9; }
    .callout.pending { border-color: var(--pending); } .callout.prepared { border-color: var(--prepared); }
    .callout b { font-weight: 500; color: var(--ink); }

    /* ── get-ready steps ── */
    ol.steps { list-style: none; counter-reset: step; margin: clamp(24px, 3vw, 36px) 0 0; padding: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }
    ol.steps > li { counter-increment: step; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 76px minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: 20px; padding: 26px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); }
    ol.steps > li::before { content: counter(step, decimal-leading-zero); grid-row: 1 / span 20; font: 400 44px/0.9 Bebas, sans-serif; background: var(--holo); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent; }
    ol.steps > li > * { grid-column: 2; max-width: 68ch; }
    ol.steps h3 { font: 800 21px/1.25 Rubik, sans-serif; margin: 0 0 8px; }
    ol.steps p { margin: 6px 0 0; color: #d5d1c9; font-size: 16px; }
    ol.steps a { text-decoration-color: #6b6862; text-underline-offset: 3px; }
    ol.steps b { font-weight: 500; color: var(--ink); }
    .ok { color: var(--mute) !important; font-size: 14.5px !important; }
    .ok::before { content: '\2713\00A0\00A0'; color: #c8ff8a; }
    .os p { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 74px 1fr; gap: 10px; }
    .os-tag { font: 500 11px/1.9 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .2em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--mute); }
    .cmd { display: flex; align-items: stretch; margin-top: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--line); background: #0f0f0e; max-width: 68ch; }
    .cmd code { scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: #3a3934 transparent; flex: 1; min-width: 0; padding: 12px 14px; background: none; font-size: 14.5px; overflow-x: auto; white-space: nowrap; }
    .copy { font: 500 11px/1 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink); background: #1a1a19; border: 0; border-inline-start: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 0 16px; cursor: pointer; }
    .copy:hover { background: #262624; } .copy.done { color: #c8ff8a; }
    .quote { font-style: italic; color: var(--ink) !important; border-left: 2px solid #b98cff; padding-left: 12px; }
    .for { font: 500 11px/1 Rubik, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #ffd36b; border: 1px solid #ffd36b; padding: 4px 7px; margin-inline-start: 8px; vertical-align: 3px; white-space: nowrap; }
    ul.folders { list-style: none; margin: 14px 0 0; padding: 0; display: grid; grid-template-rows: repeat(5, auto); grid-auto-flow: column; gap: 6px 28px; justify-content: start; font-size: 14px; }
    ul.folders li { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; }
    ul.folders span { font: 400 20px/1 Bebas, sans-serif; color: var(--faint); }
    ul.folders code { white-space: nowrap; }
    .path { font-size: 14.5px !important; color: var(--ink) !important; background: #0f0f0e; border: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 9px 12px; }

    /* ── recovery + footer ── */
    pre { margin: 12px 0 0; padding: 16px 18px; background: #0f0f0e; border: 1px solid var(--line); overflow-x: auto; font: 400 14px/1.6 ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; color: #e9e5dc; }
    footer { margin-top: clamp(64px, 9vw, 120px); border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 28px 0 40px; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
    footer img { height: 30px; width: auto; filter: invert(1); display: block; }
    footer p { margin: 0; color: var(--mute); font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: .2em; text-transform: uppercase; }

    @media (max-width: 900px) {
      .grid-4 { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
      .index { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
      article.ch { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
      .ch-side { position: static; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-end; gap: 6px 18px; }
      .ch-side .ch-terr { margin-top: 0; }
      .ch-num { font-size: 88px; }
    }
    @media (max-width: 620px) {
      ol.steps > li { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }
      ol.steps > li::before { grid-row: auto; margin-bottom: 8px; }
      ol.steps > li > * { grid-column: 1; }
      .os p { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 2px; }
      ul.folders { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; }
      @media (max-width: 340px) { ul.folders code { white-space: normal; word-break: break-all; } }
      .sec-head { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); row-gap: 6px; }
      .sec-title { font-size: clamp(26px, 8.4vw, 34px); }
      .sculpture { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; }
      body { font-size: 16px; }
      .grid-4, .index, .two-col, .facts { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }
      .dare { text-align: start; }
    }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { html { scroll-behavior: auto; } * { transition: none !important; } .brief.bi > span { filter: none !important; transform: none !important; } }
  

/* ── camera & microphone test ── */
.media-test { margin-top: 12px; max-width: 68ch; }
.media-btn { font: 500 14px/1 Rubik, sans-serif; color: #000; background: var(--holo); border: 0; padding: 13px 18px; cursor: pointer; }
.media-video { display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 360px; aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; object-fit: cover; margin-top: 12px; background: #111; transform: scaleX(-1); }
.media-video[hidden], .media-meter[hidden] { display: none; }
.media-meter { height: 6px; max-width: 360px; background: #1c1c1b; margin-top: 8px; }
.media-meter div { height: 100%; width: 0; background: var(--holo); transition: width 60ms linear; }
.media-status { font-size: 14.5px !important; color: var(--mute) !important; min-height: 1.4em; }

/* ── workshop time reminder (get-ready page) ── */
.when { margin-top: clamp(28px, 4vw, 48px); border-top: 1px solid var(--line); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); padding: clamp(18px, 2.5vw, 28px) 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 6px clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px); align-items: center; }
.when .eyebrow { grid-column: 1 / -1; margin: 0; }
.when-time { margin: 0; font: 400 clamp(44px, 7vw, 92px)/.9 Bebas, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .01em; white-space: nowrap; }
.when-time span:first-child { color: var(--ink); }
.when-note { margin: 0; color: #d5d1c9; font-size: clamp(15px, 1.4vw, 18px); max-width: 38ch; }
@media (max-width: 620px) { .when { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } .when-time span { display: block; } /* date, then the time large: two lines by design */ .when-time span:last-child { font-size: 1.5em; } }

/* ── Hebrew pages (dir="rtl") ── */
[dir="rtl"] .eyebrow, [dir="rtl"] .tag, [dir="rtl"] footer p, [dir="rtl"] .copy, [dir="rtl"] .for { letter-spacing: .04em; } /* Hebrew has no capitals; wide tracking breaks its words */
[dir="rtl"] .eyebrow { font-size: 13px; }
[dir="rtl"] .brief.bi:focus-visible { box-shadow: 14px 0 0 -12px #b98cff; }
[dir="rtl"] code, [dir="rtl"] pre, [dir="rtl"] .cmd code { direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate; text-align: left; }
[dir="rtl"] ul.folders { justify-content: start; }
[dir="rtl"] .sculpture { margin-left: 0; margin-right: calc(50% - 50vw); } /* full-bleed from the right edge in RTL */
@media (max-width: 900px) { ul.folders { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } } /* the two-column folder list doesn't fit beside the step number */

/* ── hidden notes inside a station (open on click) ── */
details.more { margin-top: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); max-width: 60ch; }
details.more + details.more { margin-top: 0; }
.needs + details.more { margin-top: 14px; }
details.more summary { cursor: pointer; list-style: none; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 12px 0; font: 500 14px/1.3 Rubik, sans-serif; color: var(--mute); }
details.more summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
details.more summary::after { content: '+'; margin-inline-start: auto; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1; color: var(--ink); }
details.more[open] summary::after { content: '\2212'; }
details.more summary:hover, details.more[open] summary { color: var(--ink); }
details.more > :not(summary) { margin: 0 0 10px; color: #d5d1c9; font-size: 15.5px; }
details.more .cmd { margin-top: 4px; max-width: 100%; }
details.more .ok { margin-top: 4px; }
article.ch > div { min-width: 0; } /* long commands scroll inside their box instead of widening the page */
[dir="rtl"] .when { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } /* the Hebrew date is longer: the note goes under it */
[dir="rtl"] .path b { white-space: nowrap; unicode-bidi: isolate; } /* each menu name stays whole and in order */
@media (max-width: 900px) { .index a:last-child:nth-child(odd) { grid-column: 1 / -1; } } /* two columns: the ninth card spans both, no empty cell */
```

### `video-day-table` — `daring-day-table.mp4` (not inlined)

Around the table on the day: a participant seated at the stations, laptops running them, someone photographing a screen with a phone in the foreground. From the owner's original `IMG_3630`, converted to H.264 where needed, then every face blurred frame by frame on this machine with macOS Vision, each detection held for 12 frames so a face Vision loses for a moment stays covered, plus timed regions added by eye after checking frames across the clip. Audio removed. Browser windows and participants' work stay visible; the owner accepted that on 2026-10-19.

## 7. Rendering contract

**Which tool presents it.** `presentation.default_component` is `show_artifact`, so when DARING is the answer the agent embeds a running station or the stations page rather than describing them. `show_artifact` is in `enabledTools` in `config/ui.config.ts`. It resolves to `ArtifactViewer`, which iframes `/api/artifact/daring-workshop/<file>` for the artifact the model names, or the first one (`stations-page`) when it names none. `show_gallery` is also enabled and renders the canonical `media[]` through `MediaGallery`. `show_video` stays disabled in config, so the three videos reach the page through `media[]` and `MediaGallery`. `show_transformation` does not apply: there are no `before_after` media.

**Artifacts and their viewports.** Every artifact is `"viewport": "desktop"`, because each one is a wide page: the stations page and the get-ready page are responsive sites, and the stations draw on a 960-pixel canvas beside a 300-pixel control column. `ArtifactViewer` renders desktop artifacts at 1280×800 and scales them to the stage; the chat column still shows them phone-portrait inline, which the two pages handle and the stations tolerate. All nine are `"sanitized": true` and `"visibility": "public"`, which is what `/api/portfolio` requires before it exposes an artifact. The order matters: `retrieval/src/peeks.ts` previews the last artifact with a `stage`, or else the first artifact, and none of these has a `stage`, so the peek shows `stations-page`.

| artifact id | label | file |
|---|---|---|
| `stations-page` | התחנות | `workshop/index.html` |
| `get-ready-page` | מתכוננים | `workshop/get-ready.html` |
| `station-01` | 01 · מילה שבורחת ממי שכתב אותה | `stations/01-typography/index.html` |
| `station-03` | 03 · חפץ בלי שם | `stations/03-object-without-name/index.html` |
| `station-05` | 05 · חומר עם זיכרון | `stations/05-material-memory/index.html` |
| `station-06` | 06 · מכונה שמוצאת הליכה | `stations/06-gait/index.html` |
| `station-07` | 07 · חלל שגדל מאחורי הדלת | `stations/07-space-behind-door/index.html` |
| `station-08` | 08 · תמונה שממציאה את מה שמחוצה לה | `stations/08-image-outside/index.html` |
| `station-09` | 09 · נול עם מוטציות | `stations/09-loom/index.html` |

**Peek copy**, from `project.json` → `peek`: hook "Nine generative-design stations. One hour. One table.", supporting "A workshop for Zemingo's designers — every station a working starter, tested before the day.", cta "Try a station".

**Media.** The package's `media[]` holds one `prototype` (`media_stations_page`), nine station `image` items (`media_station_01` … `media_station_09`), six photos from the day (`media_day_*`, `image`) and three clips from the day (`media_day_*_clip`, `video`), all public. The canonical entry's `media[]` is what the portfolio's gallery actually reads, and it carries the prototype, four of the station images (01, 03, 07, 09), all six photos and all three videos. The other five station images are reachable through the package's media ids, which the conversation hooks and `process[]` recommend. There are no `before_after` or `gallery` items. Every face in the photos and videos is blurred.

**Conversation hooks.** Three, in `project.json` → `conversation_hooks`: AI-native design leadership and team enablement (recommends the stations page, two photos and the three clips from the day); range in creative coding and generative design (stations 01, 03, 07, 09, 02, 04); and how AI-built software is directed and verified (stations 08, 05, 06). Each `agent_response_goal` keeps the claim to what is recorded: one internal workshop, reported by the owner as a success.

**The frame and its protections.** The iframe sandbox comes from `config/ui.config.ts` → `uiConfig.embedSandbox`:

```text
allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-forms
```

`allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` is deliberately absent. `allow-same-origin` is acceptable only because artifacts are first-party committed files and, in production, `ARTIFACT_ORIGIN` puts them on a separate host. The two conditions are in the config's own comment, and a rebuild must keep both. The route `apps/web/app/api/artifact/[...path]/route.ts` builds this CSP per request against the serving origin:

```text
default-src 'none'
script-src <origin> 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'
style-src <origin> 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com
font-src <origin> data: https://fonts.gstatic.com
img-src <origin> data: blob:
media-src <origin> data: blob:
connect-src <origin>
frame-ancestors 'self' <APP_ORIGIN>
base-uri 'none'
form-action 'none'
```

It also sends `x-content-type-options: nosniff` and `referrer-policy: no-referrer`, and injects a scrollbar-hiding `<style>` after `<head>` in every HTML response. Three things in this project exist because of that contract. Fonts are data URIs, because `font-src` admits `data:` and the route refuses `.woff2`. Every station uses relative paths, because a station built for `/` would ask the app root for its files. And the stations that need a microphone (02) or a camera (04) are not artifacts, because the sandbox grants neither and the camera station also needs a `.task` model and `.wasm` the route will not serve.

Rendered through the real route and sandbox on 2026-10-19 (Next dev server, Chrome), all nine artifacts loaded without a CSP violation. Two consoles show one harmless 404 each: station 08 looks for the participant's own images at `/my-images/manifest.json` and falls back to its prepared reveal, and station 09's page has no icon link, so the browser asks for `/favicon.ico`.

## 8. Rehydration

Run these from the root of a `personal_assistant` checkout. The steps assume the receiving repo has the same artifact route, registry and config as `0ca906b`; if it does not, read §7 first.

1. Create the directories:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/workshop/assets content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/workshop/source content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/gallery content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/01-typography/assets content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/03-object-without-name/assets content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/05-material-memory/assets content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/06-gait/assets content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/07-space-behind-door/assets content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/08-image-outside/assets content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/08-image-outside/prepared content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts/stations/09-loom/assets
   ```

2. Write `content/projects/daring-workshop/project.json` from the §4 block exactly, followed by one newline. The loader discovers the project as soon as this file exists.

3. Write every text asset in §6 (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, SVG) verbatim to the destination path on the line above it. Do not reformat, re-indent or tidy them, and keep the minified bundles on their original lines; the content inside each fence is the file, and the fence is longer than any run of backticks inside it.

4. Decode every raster in §6 to its destination path. Save each `data:` string as-is to a text file, then run this once per asset, with the text file and the destination path as arguments:

   ```bash
   python3 - asset.txt <destination-path> <<'PY'
import base64, sys
src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
uri = open(src).read().strip()
open(dst, 'wb').write(base64.b64decode(uri.split(',', 1)[1]))
PY
   ```

   Or have the session read this file and write each asset directly.

5. Splice the canonical records into `content/canonical/canonical-knowledge.json`. Append the §2 object to `projects[]` and the §3 records to `entities[]`, `sources[]` and `relationships[]`, skipping any id that already exists, and append the `generated_by` clause from §3. Keep the file's formatting (2-space indent, non-ASCII unescaped, trailing newline):

   ```bash
   python3 -c "import json;p='content/canonical/canonical-knowledge.json';d=json.load(open(p));open(p,'w').write(json.dumps(d,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)+'\n')"
   ```

6. Copy the three videos into `apps/web/public/media/` with the names in the manifest. They come from the source checkout at `apps/web/public/media/daring-day-*.mp4`; they are not in this file. Use those blurred files; never re-export them from the originals.

7. Verify the bytes against the manifest. Every line must match a sha256 in §5; there must be 45 artifact files and three videos:

   ```bash
   (cd content/projects/daring-workshop/artifacts && find . -type f | sort | xargs shasum -a 256)
   shasum -a 256 apps/web/public/media/daring-day-*.mp4
   ```

8. Validate, then restart the dev server, because knowledge is cached at boot:

   ```bash
   npm run knowledge:validate
   ```

   On a fresh clone, build `@par/config` first (`npm run build --workspace=@par/config`), or every API route returns 500.

9. Check it renders. `GET /api/artifact/daring-workshop/workshop/index.html` and each `…/stations/<nn>/index.html` should return 200 with the CSP in §7, and `/api/portfolio` should list `project_daring_workshop` with nine artifacts and the thumbnail `/api/artifact/daring-workshop/thumb.jpg`. Open one station in the conversation and press Start. The three videos should resolve under `/media/`.

10. Record the change in `docs/knowledge/`. The source repo's record is `docs/knowledge/project-daring-workshop-v0.1.md`.

## 9. Conventions for a new project

These are the rules this project follows, written so they apply to the next one.

**Ids and names.** The canonical id is `project_<snake_case>`, and `project.json` → `id` is the same canonical id. The kebab-case slug is only the directory name, `content/projects/<kebab-slug>/`, and the URL segment in `/api/artifact/<kebab-slug>/…`. Every project in the repo is built this way, whatever an outside brief says about the package id. Artifact ids are short kebab-case (`stations-page`, `station-07`). Media ids are `media_<snake_case>`. New tools are entities `tool_<snake_case>` with `type: "tool"`; new sources are `source_<what>_<yyyy_mm_dd>`.

**Where files go.** Anything the artifact route serves goes under `content/projects/<slug>/artifacts/`, in subfolders when a page has its own relative `assets/`. `file` is then a relative path such as `stations/09-loom/index.html`. Video goes to `apps/web/public/media/<slug-prefix>-<name>.mp4` and is referenced as `/media/…`, because the route has no video content type. Fonts cannot be shipped as `.woff2` or `.woff`: inline them in the CSS as `data:font/woff2;base64,…`.

**Built work.** When the work is a built app (Vite, or anything with a bundler), build it with relative paths (`--base ./`), copy the output, and check every file extension against the route's list before committing. Anything the route refuses (`.wav`, `.wasm`, `.task`, fonts) either gets inlined or means the piece cannot be an artifact; show it as an image instead and say why in `open_questions`. Look for absolute paths in the bundle (`/something`) — they resolve against the app, not the artifact. Test every artifact through the real route inside an iframe with the configured sandbox, from a page on the app's origin; opening the route URL directly skips the sandbox, and framing from another artifact response inherits that response's CSP.

**Register twice.** `project.json` gives the agent its evidence, hooks, artifacts, process and peek. The canonical entry gives the portfolio its card, its gallery media, its thumbnail and its verification state. The gallery reads canonical `media[]`, so an item that exists only in the package never reaches the gallery. Canonical media carry no ids; package media carry ids so hooks and process steps can point at them.

**Choosing `default_component`.** Use `show_artifact` when the project owns something that runs — a page, a prototype, a tool — because using it beats being told about it. Use `media_gallery` when the evidence is a live external site or a set of images. Use `case_study_panel` when the story is process. Use `project_card` when there is little to show. The schema's enum lists only the older names; `show_artifact` is what the projects that embed use.

**`viewport`.** `"mobile"` for a phone UI designed at phone width, where a desktop frame would stretch it. `"desktop"` for anything wide: a site, a canvas-and-controls tool, a recording, a presentation page. Either way the chat column shows it phone-portrait inline, so build pages responsive.

**`peek` copy.** Three short lines. The hook says what the visitor can do or see, in a few words ("Nine generative-design stations. One hour. One table."). The supporting line names the work concretely; no adjective stands in for a fact. The cta is a two-or-three-word verb phrase for what the preview invites ("Try a station").

**`evidence[]`.** One entry per real thing. `notes` says exactly what it contains, where it lives and why it is or is not linked. `verified` only for what was read directly or said by the owner; owner statements go in a dated `manual_confirmation` entry that records what was said and nothing more. A private company repository is `uri: null` with the reason in the notes.

**Whose work it is.** A repository can hold work by more than one person. Read the commit authors before building artifacts from it, present only the owner's work as his, and build from the last commit that is his when others changed the same files later. Say so in the package and in canonical `notes`.

**People in media.** Photos and videos of colleagues or participants go public only with every face blurred, and only when the owner decides so; record the decision and its date in `evidence[]`, and keep a visitor-safe `open_questions` line about consent. Blur on the machine, never through an online service. Automatic face detection misses turned and down-looking faces, so check every photo and frames across every clip by eye and add regions by hand; a video counts as showing faces if any frame does. Faces on screens count too (webcam previews, a woven or printed portrait), and so does anything on screen that names a confidential client. Strip audio unless it is the point. Ship only the blurred files and say in the package that the originals must never be re-exported.

**Verification.** A project drafted from sources rather than reviewed by the owner is `status: "draft"` in the package and `verification_status: "needs_verification"` in canonical, even when individual facts are confirmed. Both flip only after the owner reads the copy.

**Artifacts are the work.** Copy them byte for byte. Make only edits the platform forces, list each one in §6 of the package and in the decision record, and mark `sanitized: true` only after reviewing the files for personal data. An artifact without `sanitized: true` never reaches a visitor.

## 10. Provenance and gaps

**Status.** Package `status: "draft"`, canonical `verification_status: "needs_verification"`. The project was added on 2026-10-19 at the owner's request. The facts come from the workshop repository (`source_daring_workshop_repo_2026_10_19`) and from what the owner said in the Claude Code sessions that built the workshop (`source_owner_statements_daring_2026_10`, `evidence_owner_statements`). On 2026-10-19 he confirmed his role — Design Team Leader and workshop facilitator — and that he designed the workshop, including the key visual and the 3D ribbon, and wrote its content. The rest of the prose was drafted from those sources and has not been reviewed by him, so the status stays draft.

**Open questions**, quoted from the package:

- Attendance and the participants' own results from the day are not recorded.
- Faces in the photos and videos from the day are blurred; the participants' consent to publication is not recorded.
- The second run for another team (planned for about a week after 6 October 2026) is not recorded as having happened.
- Stations 02 (microphone) and 04 (camera, with a MediaPipe model and WebAssembly the artifact route does not serve) cannot run inside the portfolio's sandboxed frame, so they appear only as images.

**Sanitisation.** None of these artifacts passed through `scripts/import-artifacts.ts`; its substitution map belongs to the internship platform's bundle. They were reviewed by hand: the pages and stations contain no personal names or addresses. The repository URL `bitbucket.org/zemingo/daring-workshop` appears in the get-ready page's instructions; it names Zemingo's private repository and gives no access. The edits made, all forced by the platform, are four. Fonts were inlined into `workshop/style.css` and station 01's CSS, with the `.woff` fallbacks removed. Station 08's prepared-images path changed from `/prepared` to `./prepared`. Stations were built with `--base ./`. Stations 06 and 09 were built from `e519810` rather than `main`. Faces in the six photos and three videos from the day were blurred on this machine (macOS Vision plus regions added by eye), with the webcam preview, the woven portrait and the bookmark bar naming a confidential client in the photos; audio was removed from the videos. A rebuild must start from the files in this package.

**The 3D shape.** The DARING ribbon travels in two forms: `workshop/assets/hero.js`, the compiled bundle the pages run, and `workshop/source/hero.js` with its build config, the readable source to change it from. The poster it was built after is `workshop/assets/poster.webp`, and `thumb.jpg` is a still of the live shape.

**Not carried over.** The thank-you page is left out; its photos and videos are in the gallery instead, blurred. The originals of those photos and videos are not carried over and must not be. Stations 02 and 04 are left out as runnable artifacts, for the device and file-type reasons in §7. The participants' later changes to 04, 06 and 09 are left out, because they are theirs. The workshop repository's tests, harness and `REPORT.md` are not copied; they are cited as evidence.

**Schema drift, for the next reader.** `schemas/project-evidence-schema-v0.1.json` does not define the top-level `artifacts` or `peek` keys, and its `presentation.default_component` enum does not include `show_artifact`. Every embedding project uses them anyway, and `knowledge:validate` checks only the runtime invariants (a short pitch, some evidence, verified evidence before publishing), so this package follows the content, not the schema. The brief that asked for this package also said `project.json`'s id is the kebab slug; in this repo it is the canonical id, and this package follows the repo.

**Checks run on 2026-10-19.** `npm run knowledge:validate` passes with 11 project packages. `npm run eval` gives 31/33, and the same two cases (`starter_default_tell_me_about_boaz`, `starter_returning_pick_up_where_we_left_off`) fail on the committed tree without this project. All 48 manifest entries were hashed from the files on disk (25997209 bytes). Nothing is committed.
